flawed_step: After fixing a closed set C and x∉C, the standard proof would apply normality to C and {x}. This is unjustified because, without a T1 assumption, {x} need not be closed.
counterexample: Let X={0,1} with topology τ={∅,{1},X}. Its closed sets are ∅,{0},X. It is normal: any two disjoint closed sets must include ∅, and they can be enclosed in the disjoint open sets ∅ and X. But it is not regular under the given definition. Take C={0} and x=1. Every open set containing C is X, while every open set containing x is either {1} or X; neither is disjoint from X. Thus no disjoint open U,V satisfy 1∈U and C⊆V.
assessment_summary: The proof attempt fails when normality is applied to the point singleton, since singletons need not be closed. The two-point Sierpiński space above is normal but fails the stated definition of regularity, so the statement is false without T1.
